subject: Clarify: default retention for streamed tokens vs final outputs (EU residency)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finovia.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Default retention for streaming tokens vs final outputs (Finovia compliance question)

Hi Grace,

Quick question from our security/compliance team as we evaluate Redwood for a pilot: what does Redwood retain by default for interactive sessions? Specifically:

- If we use streaming (token-by-token) for a chat UI, do streaming tokens get written to logs by default, or only final assembled outputs?
- How long are request items (prompts / user inputs) retained vs model-generated outputs?
- We need confirmation the EU pilot will keep retained artifacts inside EU boundaries by default (and what the erasure workflow looks like) — can you share a brief summary and any supporting artifacts (SOC2 snapshot, erasure checklist etc.)?

We have an internal timeline to sign the pilot contract in October, so any concise clarification would be helpful.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Vendor Risk
Finovia Bank

(attachment: SOC2-snapshot.pdf)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finovia.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Default retention for streaming tokens vs final outputs (Finovia compliance question)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by a few operational notes.

Short answers:
- Streaming tokens: not stored by default. Our runtime can stream tokens to the client without persisting the token stream unless the customer enables "record_streams" in their project settings or explicitly opts into debug logging.
- Requests (prompts / user inputs): retained by default for 30 days. This covers the raw request payloads used for debugging/quality and for supporting customer-initiated erasure flows.
- Model-generated outputs (final assembled responses): retained by default for 90 days. We keep outputs longer than inputs to support offline quality monitoring, regression detection, and to allow customers to request debug snapshots if an issue is reported.
- EU residency: for accounts configured with EU residency, all logs and stored artifacts are written to EU-hosted storage by default and are not replicated to outside regions without explicit customer opt-in.

Operational notes:
- Erasure workflow: customers can file an erasure request through the Console or via support. Standard processing timeline is 72 hours for execution and verification for non-legal holds; we remove objects from active stores and then trigger our standard purge job (background TTL) which clears tombstoned records within 7 days. Metadata (audit id, request receipt) is preserved for compliance traceability but contains no PII content.
- Legal/data-hold exceptions: if a legal hold is in place, artifacts are excluded from purge until the hold is lifted. We provide a signed attestation for hold states when requested.
- Attachments: I attached our SOC2 snapshot (redacted) to this reply; Kimberly, can you confirm whether the SOC2 excerpt we provided includes the EU data residency section?

If you want, we can provide a one-page policy blurb you can attach to procurement paperwork. Also happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your InfoSec team next week.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sales, Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Default retention for streaming tokens vs final outputs (Finovia compliance question)

Grace / Kimberly — quick internal note to suggest tidy, procurement-ready wording and to confirm implementation details. Proposed bullets for the one-pager to send to Finovia: 

- Data residency: "For customers electing EU residency, all request and response artifacts stored by Redwood are persisted to EU-only storage and are not exported outside the EU unless explicitly requested by the customer."
- Default retention windows: "Requests (raw prompts/user inputs): 30 days. Generated outputs (assembled final responses): 90 days. Streaming token payloads are not persisted unless the customer enables recording."
- Erasure SLA: "Standard erasure requests are acknowledged within 24 hours and completed within 72 hours, excluding records under legal hold. Tombstoned records are purged by automatic background jobs within 7 days of erasure completion."
- Exceptions: "Customers may request a custom retention profile (shorter/longer) under an enterprise contract; changes require configuration and may affect observability/diagnostic capabilities."

Kimberly — can you attach the erasure_request_template.docx and confirm whether legal attestation text needs any legal review before sharing?

Thanks,
Jonas
